races.name: Newark Advertiser Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Bondi
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 310 days off for Declan Carroll, who has no wins from nine runners in the 14-day window; zero wins and zero places from eight runs on similar going makes the layoff and surface record a double concern.
runners_data.comment: A long absence of 310 days is the immediate concern with Bondi, and his two most recent efforts — sixth and eighth — make him hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, though he has run over today's trip and won twice in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer with strong trainer angle — Henrietta Knight running 1/1 in the 14-day window — and has won on this course and Standard going (1W1P from 15 similar-going runs); the step back down from marathon trips to 1m4f looks sensible.
runners_data.comment: Motazzen showed he can find the winner's enclosure when landing a win three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 81 underlines his claims here; the chief concern is a 82-day absence and two below-par runs since that victory.

runners_data.name: Jindri
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam sends this four-year-old here with a sharp 3/11 recent trainer strike rate; a natural hold-up horse by record who will likely find himself pushed forward into mid-division against instinct, which the style-fit flag suggests may blunt his chance.
runners_data.comment: Ran well to finish second two starts back, and she has distance and going experience in her favour, but that ninth last time out is a concern and 134 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Typical Woman
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner whose last six runs include a win over this trip on Good ground; naturally a hold-up performer, the crowded rear of this field means she will probably race in a middle position she has not chosen, and her sim-going record (0W1P from 15) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Typical Woman won four starts back but has posted three sixth-place finishes in her most recent outings, and 86 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and the step up in weight to 133 lb won't help her cause.

runners_data.name: Gallant Lion
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Typical Woman, also from Ian Williams; won over 12f on Good going but his Standard-going figures (0W1P from 15 runs) are uninspiring, and being pushed away from his preferred late-running berth further softens the appeal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four of his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Gallant Lion faces a stiff task here, though a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement after 58 days off carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old for Harriet Bethell who has won twice in the last five runs, most recently over 10f; steps up to 1m4f for the first time and the trip looks a logical target, but no Standard-going or Southwell form to reference.
runners_data.comment: Domination showed his class when winning two starts back, and third last time out keeps him in the mix, but 38 days off and a hefty 130 lb to carry are the checks on his claims here.

runners_data.name: Astrological
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides this Marco Botti-trained three-year-old who has won on Southwell's Standard surface and holds a solid Southwell place record (1W3P from 4 sim-going runs); the prominent style suits tracking Naples and the course form is the key credential.
runners_data.comment: Astrological won last time out and has run over today's trip and conditions, but 55 days off the track introduces a fitness query and he carries 130 lb against in-form rivals.

runners_data.name: Cliff Danger
runners_data.note: Pam Sly runner with just one start in the 14-day window and recent form figures of 6479; the two runs on Standard going produced a placed effort but overall form is uninspiring and he drops in from weaker fields.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Cliff Danger faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's going before and 42 days off may have freshened him up.

runners_data.name: Wonder
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old carries the deepest Southwell AW profile in the field with 14 runs on this surface returning 2W9P — a remarkable place rate; returning after 111 days but the track record speaks loudly, and apprentice Taryn Langley (5lb claim) could be a factor.
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of his last five starts, Wonder has solid recent form to call on, with a win four starts back and a pair of seconds before his latest third — he has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating has him as the top-ranked runner here; the main concern is the 111-day absence.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Champion
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old arrives over a trip he has rarely tried — recent runs have all been over shorter — and the Standard-going record reads just 0W0P from four visits; the step up in distance is a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Mehmas Champion is hard to fancy despite having run over today's going before; the 58-day absence and a hefty 144 lb burden add further questions.

runners_data.name: Yaa Min
runners_data.note: Jack Callan partners this consistent Jack Burton-trained mare who has two wins and four places from 11 runs on similar going; her prominent style should see her tracking Naples naturally and the solid course form (3/12f/STA and 1/12f/STA in the last five) is relevant.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed form in his last two starts makes Yaa Min an appealing each-way prospect, and he arrives fit enough after 45 days off having run over today's trip and going before; third last time out and third two starts back, he steps up on an official mark of 79 with our figures rating him higher.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner for Steph Hollinshead and Dougie Costello; recent form shows a 1 on debut on this surface followed by non-completions and mid-pack finishes on turf, and her last run over this trip at Southwell produced a 12th — the key question is whether she can replicate her winning front-running display or if the field catches her late.
runners_data.comment: Naples shaped with promise when third two starts back, and his rating of 85 underlines his quality in this field; the main concern is a 53-day absence heading into today's test.

races.paceDynamic: Naples is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, Dougie Costello can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits from the front, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m4f on Standard Fibresand at Southwell. The prominent types Motazzen, Astrological, Yaa Min, and Cliff Danger will line up just behind and create a sensible tracking group, meaning the pace is unlikely to collapse into a complete crawl but equally unlikely to be truly searching. Jindri, Typical Woman, and Gallant Lion are genuine hold-up horses by nature but all three are redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply too much hold-up preference in this field for them all to find their true position at the rear — of those, Jindri and Gallant Lion are most likely to actually secure a rear berth, with Typical Woman probably slotting into a middle pack role against her instincts. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Naples at close range and pounce in the straight, as well as any truly effective hold-up performer who possesses genuine finishing speed on this surface — Wonder, with 14 runs on this going and an exceptional place record, is the archetypal profile the shape is built for.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Naples leads at a sustainable clip and the prominent trackers Astrological, Motazzen, or Yaa Min press forward to challenge in the straight without triggering a war.
scenarios.body: Naples sets a metronomic pace that suits horses travelling smoothly just off the lead, and as the race develops in the home straight the cleanest passage comes to those who have tracked within two or three lengths all race; this is a textbook Southwell scenario where position-savers exploit a steady early tempo and class asserts late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to create a proper stamina test and the midfield/rear division finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: Wonder has the best Southwell record in the field by some distance — 14 runs on this going with two wins and nine places — and a steady-to-honest pace over 1m4f on this flat track is exactly the kind of contest that allows a proven finishing horse to peel wide and collect; Domination, who has won on two of his last five starts, also carries the profile of a progressive type with improving form that can sweep past tired rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Hits Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Naples is allowed to quicken the pace mid-race and the prominent group cannot sustain the effort, leaving tired horses standing in the straight.
scenarios.body: A fast-finishing prominent who can switch off early and then respond to a gear change benefits most here; Astrological has both Southwell and Standard-going form and has won on this course, giving him the tactical profile to absorb a mid-race injection of pace and still find extra late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced hold-up horses fail to settle into their unnatural midfield positions and create traffic issues that compromise multiple runners late.
scenarios.body: Typical Woman and Gallant Lion, both racing out of their natural roles and carrying the style-fit discount, may unsettle the midfield group and cause interference in the straight, handing the race to a horse who finds clean daylight early; this low-probability shape still favours a horse with a wide draw or jockey who seeks outer running room early.

watchPoints.text: Naples — if she is allowed to stride clear uncontested in the early stages and sets a deceptively slow tempo, the race may be decided too far from home for the hold-up brigade to close, fundamentally altering the outcome for Wonder and Domination.

Typical Woman and Gallant Lion — both genuine hold-up types displaced into midfield by the race shape; either could unsettle the middle pack if they fail to settle, and any traffic incident in a 12-runner field on a flat surface at a turning track affects multiple rivals.

Wonder — the 111-day absence for James Fanshawe's horse is worth monitoring; despite an outstanding Southwell record the fitness question is real, and apprentice Taryn Langley has not ridden this course extensively.

Astrological — Marco Botti's three-year-old has the best combination of Southwell course form and prominent style in the field; watch whether Marco Ghiani slots him immediately behind Naples at the break, as that single tactical decision could define his race.

Mehmas Champion — significant step up in trip for a horse whose recent runs have all been over 8f on soft and good ground; if he fails to settle over the unfamiliar 1m4f distance, David Nolan may find himself stranded in the midfield with no finishing kick when it counts.

races.name: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love You More
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a win and a place on Standard Southwell AW (sim-going: 7/14, 1W1P) and a course victory in her form string; Jack Callan takes the ride for Joseph Parr, whose yard is 0/4 in the last 14 days — 34 days off is manageable and the course-going angle is the main positive.|
runners_data.comment: Three losses sandwiching a win in her last five starts make Love You More inconsistent at best, and ranked eleventh of fourteen on our figures she faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 133 lb from stall eight, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Implied Volatility
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare who has finished no better than seventh in her last five starts including two on this course, carrying a 0W0P record on similar going across 11 attempts — the form line offers little encouragement and there is no obvious angle for improvement today.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unplaced in the two most recent, Implied Volatility faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a 41-day break may have freshened him up from stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: The Spotlight Kid
runners_data.note: A confirmed closer with 14 runs on similar going including five placings from that sample, and strong Southwell AW course form; the crowded hold-up division means Rob Hornby may struggle to get the back-of-the-field position this horse genuinely needs, and its chance must be tempered by the likelihood of racing closer to the pace than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Spotlight Kid does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third two starts back shows he can get competitive; at 131 lb from stall 11, however, he faces a stiff ask to break that duck here.

runners_data.name: Create
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up type who recorded back-to-back wins on Good and returned a place on that surface, but has limited success on Standard AW (2W4P from 8 runs on similar going, though recent form shows 12th placings); Kieran O'Neill rides and the horse is bumped toward midfield on the map — its natural home is towards the rear, and its best chance depends on getting a clear run in a race where space will be at a premium.|
runners_data.comment: Create shaped up well on her latest start to score, and having already run over today's trip and going, conditions pose no fresh questions. She carries 131 lb from stall 14, but her recent winning fitness makes her our pick here.

runners_data.name: Heretic
runners_data.note: Well-travelled seven-year-old with an excellent record on similar going (13/15 runs, 2W5P) and genuine proven ability at this level; David Probert rides and the horse wears a tp headgear combination; true to its nature a hold-up runner who is more comfortable at the back, though the compressed field means it may be closer than ideal — the strong AW pace record is the key positive.|
runners_data.comment: Heretic has been consistently placed in recent starts, finishing second and third in his last two outings, and has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is that he has been off the track for 66 days and is yet to score.

runners_data.name: Tardaff
runners_data.note: Well-weighted at OR 55 but limited Southwell form — only 1 run on similar going from 8 opportunities — and Billy Loughnane cannot compensate for a horse that simply does not have a proven course profile; the recent form figures of 005 on Good ground are not encouraging, and the hold-up style is likely to leave it adrift of a controlled pace.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tardaff has at least run over today's trip and comes here fresh enough on 17 days' rest, but a fifth last time out and little improvement in recent outings make her a modest each-way proposition at best from stall four carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Ribston Pippin
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the pivotal horse in this race's shape; Darragh Keenan rides for Lemos De Souza (2/7 in the past 14 days) and the horse won on Standard AW at this trip, holding up a 8/15 similar-going record (1W3P); the STYLE_FIT flag reflects a horse that is technically listed as prominent but whose confirmed role as race leader means it races fully within its profile today — the question is whether the moderate gallop it sets suits it to the line.|
runners_data.comment: Ribston Pippin landed a win and posted a second in his last five starts, but has disappointed in his two most recent outings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and at 134 lb from stall seven, a return to form after 29 days off would be needed to make an impact.

runners_data.name: Barleybrown
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (p) who sits prominently enough in the field to track Ribston Pippin from a good position; P J McDonald is a powerful booking for Ruth Carr, and 7 runs on similar going yielding 2 places suggests competence without dominance on the AW surface — 52 days off is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Barleybrown brings useful experience over today's distance and going, and our rating ranks him top of the 14 — second two starts back highlights his capability, though he has been winless in his last six and that latest eighth is the concern.

runners_data.name: Mercurius Power
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer with an outstanding similar-going record of 13/15 runs and 5 places from that sample, and a place in his most recent run on Standard Southwell; Ray Dawson rides and tp headgear is applied — ideally drawn to take full advantage of a controlled pace set by Ribston Pippin and is tactically the best-placed of the pack.|
runners_data.comment: Mercurius Power returns on a sharp 22-day turnaround having posted a runner-up finish last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; ranked second of 14 on our ratings, the chief risk is his failure to convert, winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Splinterwood
runners_data.note: A young four-year-old with only 4 runs on similar going (all returning outside the places on Standard AW) and no wins or places in that sample; Daniel Muscutt takes the ride for Michael Appleby but form reads 7-679 and this horse, a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield by necessity, faces a stiff task getting competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Splinterwood has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his finishing positions have been modest throughout and a trainer in lean form — just one success from 21 runners in the past fortnight — does little to inspire confidence despite the low draw at stall two.

runners_data.name: Have You A Minute
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with wins over further (10f, Standard AW) who has been campaigned almost exclusively at 10f and steps back to a mile today — the trip shortening is a genuine concern; Hector Crouch rides for Tom Tate (0/1 in 14 days) and 61 days off adds an element of freshness risk; its best form is at longer distances, which tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Have You A Minute faces a stiff task from stall 12 off 61 days, though he has run over today's distance and going before and does at least bring a win in recent form.

runners_data.name: Muddy Marvellous
runners_data.note: Returning from 257 days off — by far the longest layoff in this field — and carries a finishes-fade warning flag alongside a 0W0P record across 5 runs on similar going; Dale Swift rides for Seb Spencer (1/6 in 14 days) and the combination of a very extended absence, a tendency to fade in the finish, and the positional congestion in the hold-up group makes this an extremely difficult proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 257 days, Muddy Marvellous faces a stiff task as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a featherweight draw from stall one offers at least a neutral starting point.

runners_data.name: Timebar
runners_data.note: A hold-up five-year-old with a useful placing record (0W2P from 10 similar-going runs) and headgear (t); Jack G Gilligan rides for Roy Bowring (2/5 in 14 days) — recent form includes two second-place finishes at shorter trips (7f, 6f) which means stepping back up to a mile is a legitimate question mark, though a front-runner-dominated pace may actually help horses who stay on.|
runners_data.comment: Timebar has been consistently placed, finishing second three times in his last five starts, though he remains yet to win in recent form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a 22-day break looks fair enough, though 129 lb from stall nine may test his resolution.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who wears tp headgear and has run predominantly on Good or Soft ground over 8-9f; Duran Fentiman rides for Tim Easterby (5/70 in 14 days, a strong recent strike rate) and the horse has been placed on Good at 9f — the switch to Standard AW at one mile is an untested combination, and recent form figures of 296906 do not inspire confidence without surface confirmation.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Evelyn's Phoenix faces a stiff task here; sixth last time out and largely out of the frame in recent outings, he does have experience over today's trip and returns on a handy 15-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Ribston Pippin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from a rival willing to take them on from the gates — they should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on this flat Southwell AW mile without being harried. Behind them, Mercurius Power and Barleybrown are the natural prominent types best placed to track the leader through the early and middle sectors, while the remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses. The field carries a significant volume of genuine hold-up types — The Spotlight Kid, Heretic, Create, Splinterwood, Have You A Minute, Timebar, Muddy Marvellous, and Evelyn's Phoenix are all true closers who have been pushed forward on the pace map because there is simply no room for all of them at the back; in reality, several will be unable to adopt their natural position and may find themselves shuffled wide or crowded. With a single front-runner dictating a moderate, uncontested tempo on a flat circuit, the pace shape strongly favours horses tracking close to the leader — prominent and close-up racing positions — rather than those relying on a true end-to-end gallop to set up a late rush from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ribston Pippin Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ribston Pippin leads from the break without pressure and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits close trackers.
scenarios.body: Ribston Pippin dictates throughout at a comfortable tempo, with Mercurius Power and Barleybrown sitting in the slipstream and poised to challenge in the final furlong; the lack of genuine pace pressure means the front two or three in the field are never truly tested until the finish. Prominent racers who conserve energy by sitting close to an uncontested leader gain the clearest tactical advantage, and hold-up horses left with too much ground to make up from deep will find the moderate gallop insufficient to generate the late sectionals they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ribston Pippin's uncontested lead proves slightly too comfortable and close-tracking rivals swamp them inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Barleybrown and Mercurius Power, both patient prominent types with strong Southwell AW form, are ideally placed to pounce when the pace naturally quickens in the closing stages; with no mid-race injection of tempo, they arrive with energy preserved. This is the natural runner-up scenario to Scenario A — the same pace shape, slightly different outcome at the line — and benefits the same tracking profiles rather than deep closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than anticipated, burning off the prominent horses and leaving enough of a searching pace to allow true hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: The Spotlight Kid and Heretic, both proven at Southwell AW with strong similar-going records, are the hold-up types most likely to produce a late run if the tempo genuinely tests the field; however, several closers have been redistributed out of their natural position and may be unable to get the clear passage they need. This scenario is structurally less likely because the pace map shows no second front-runner to pressurize Ribston Pippin, and many of the nominal mid-field horses are natural closers forced forward — the finish from deep requires conditions this race shape is unlikely to produce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If a troubled or muddled run causes traffic issues mid-race, scrambling the field and producing a random winner from a crowded, disorganised pack.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners on a flat one-mile circuit and a large cluster of hold-up horses occupying similar ground, positional crowding in the back straight is a real logistical risk; a horse that finds an unlikely clear run or benefits from a gap could arrive late from an unexpected position. Love You More, who won on this course and going combination, could be the beneficiary if gaps open, though this scenario hinges on race-day chaos rather than a predictable pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Mercurius Power is the most tactically advantaged horse in the race — 13 starts on similar going with 5 places, Ray Dawson booked, and a natural prominent style that puts it right behind an uncontested Ribston Pippin; if the lead horse sets an easy gallop, Mercurius Power is best placed to pounce.

Ribston Pippin controls the race shape entirely — watch whether Darragh Keenan attempts to inject an early injection of pace or switches to a conserving front-running role, as that decision will determine whether deep closers have any chance of reaching them.

Positional crowding in the back straight is a real risk with seven or eight genuine hold-up types all looking for similar ground behind a single leader — watch for trouble in running around the final bend, particularly involving The Spotlight Kid, Heretic, and Create who all want the same late-run position.

Muddy Marvellous returns from 257 days off and carries a fade-in-finish flag — watch how it travels through the first half as an indicator of condition; if it weakens early it could cause interference for the closers immediately behind it.

Have You A Minute steps back from 10f to 1m for the first time in its recent profile — watch the early stages to see whether Hector Crouch attempts to compensate for the trip drop by hunting a closer position than the horse's natural hold-up style would ordinarily dictate.

races.name: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (Div I) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Assiri Heights
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old returns after 389 days off — a significant layoff flag — having shaped with some promise at Goodwood; a true hold-up horse whose chance depends entirely on getting a clear run from what will be a congested midfield position forced upon it by the race shape.

runners_data.name: Blue Boy Junior
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners a horse whose last two starts came on Soft and Good ground over seven furlongs; the step up to a mile on Standard Fibresand is an open question, and though naturally inclined to race from the rear, he will find himself racing closer to the pace than ideal given the lack of other front-runners to fill that berth.

runners_data.name: Jetpack Jimmy
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's charge has a single run on Standard going and finished tenth over seven furlongs in that appearance — limited evidence to build a case on; carries a "fades in finish" flag and, squeezed into midfield when his instinct is to race further back, the combination of style displacement and that stamina query is a concern.

runners_data.name: Mercantile
runners_data.note: The sole unknown quantity in the race — no form string, going labelled UNKNOWN, and a lightly raced profile that makes assessment near-impossible; Daniel and Claire Kubler have shown a respectable 14-day strike rate at 6/17, so a fit, freshly prepared runner cannot be dismissed entirely even without a form anchor.

runners_data.name: Palladas
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's three-year-old won over eight furlongs on Standard going last time — directly relevant form — and the yard's 14-day record of 10/23 is strong; a natural prominent runner who should slot comfortably into second or third position behind Star of The Desert, giving him a clean sightline to the prize.

runners_data.name: Cullinan Wolf
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's four-year-old has two recent runs on similar going, finishing seventh and eighth, so proven exposure to Fibresand-style surfaces but without reward; a genuine hold-up operator mapped to midfield, his best chance is a strong pace that strings the field — which this shape does not readily promise.

runners_data.name: Wats On Tiger
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag having beaten just two rivals over a mile on Good ground last time, and Faye McManoman takes a claiming allowance; a true rear-runner who will struggle if the pace is moderate and the race becomes a sprint from the home turn, which is the most likely scenario here.

runners_data.name: Salvezza
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old ran respectably in fifth over eight furlongs at Goodwood 17 days ago — recent and relevant — and Kieran Shoemark is a high-quality booking; though a natural hold-up type pressed into midfield by the race shape, Shoemark's positional intelligence gives this horse the best chance of any redistributed runner of engineering a clean passage.

runners_data.name: Star of The Desert
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's three-year-old is the confirmed lone front-runner and holds a second-placed finish on Standard Fibresand in her form — the most directly relevant course experience in this field; tagged STYLE_FIT because her usual prominent role becomes a lead role here, and at a controlled tempo she could prove very hard to peg back if she gets away uncontested.

runners_data.name: Wyvill
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' three-year-old has two runs on Standard going, both resulting in sixth place, over ten and eight furlongs respectively; a hold-up horse who will again find himself in midfield against his natural preference, and the step back to a mile after a ten-furlong run last time is worth monitoring — the shorter trip may catch him out if he needs time to wind up.

runners_data.name: Regal Desire
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; had Regal Desire taken part, her two placed efforts on Standard and Good ground over eight furlongs would have made her one of the more interesting prominent types — her absence leaves Star of The Desert with even less pressure early, reinforcing the controlled-tempo scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Star of The Desert is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, she should bowl along at a controlled, self-set tempo on the Southwell Fibresand over one mile on Standard ground. Palladas and Regal Desire (non-runner) are the only other prominent types, meaning Star of The Desert faces minimal early pressure and can dictate a pace that is honest but not searingly fast — the kind that rewards horses who travel comfortably just off the pace rather than those forced to make up vast ground late. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate: Jetpack Jimmy, Cullinan Wolf, Blue Boy Junior, Assiri Heights, Wyvill, Salvezza and Wats On Tiger all have natural rear-running tendencies but several will be shuffled into an uncharacteristic midfield berth simply because there is nowhere else to go. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled front-running tempo with a compressed midfield suits prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel smoothly into contention from the home turn — horses who need a truly searching gallop to deliver their best are disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Star of The Desert dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the winner tracks her comfortably before kicking from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Star of The Desert sets a sustainable fractions that keeps the field compact, allowing a horse sitting two or three off the pace to glide past with a clean run; the tempo is never truly taxing, so hold-up horses get little cut in the ground to exploit late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to soften the leaders and a hold-up runner finds an unobstructed run into the straight.
scenarios.body: A moderate crawl suddenly becomes a sprint home and one of the redistributed hold-up types — in reality racing midfield rather than their preferred rear — benefits from a clean passage; Salvezza or Assiri Heights, both trained by capable handlers, would be the likeliest to capitalise if the run materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Midfield Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If Palladas pushes up to press Star of The Desert and the tempo rises sufficiently to string the field out.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely run mile stretches the midfield and turns the race into a test of stamina and class, favouring horses with the ability to sustain their effort through the final two furlongs; Palladas, with a winning run on similar Standard going in his form, is best placed to handle a stronger gallop given his proximity to the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield creates traffic issues and a fresh, lightly-raced horse threads through late with a clear run.
scenarios.body: With so many horses redistributed into an awkward midfield cluster, a fluent mover who avoids trouble could steal a march; Mercantile, unknown quantity but lightly raced and trained by a yard in form, represents the wildcard profile that benefits most when the pace scenario is scrambled.

watchPoints.text: Star of The Desert faces zero front-running rivals — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along entirely unchallenged into the first bend, as an uncontested lead at this track over one mile is a significant advantage.

The midfield cluster will be densely packed with seven natural hold-up horses compressed into a small space — watch for traffic trouble in the straight, particularly around Salvezza and Assiri Heights who need a clear run to show their best.

Palladas returns after 200 days off for Charlie Appleby; watch the market closely in the morning — if the yard has him cherry-ripe, his Standard-going winning form makes him a standout in this pace shape, but fitness is a genuine unknown at that absence.

Wats On Tiger and Jetpack Jimmy both carry "fades in finish" flags in a race where the pace is likely to be moderate — watch whether either capitulates quickly once the field rounds the home turn and the race quickens, potentially causing interference to horses drawn near them.

Mercantile is a complete unknown with no going or form data — watch the pre-race show and any market move; an unexposed three-year-old from a yard firing at 35% over 14 days deserves monitoring even without a form line to assess.

races.name: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (Div II) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Al Jolson
runners_data.note: Debut runner for the powerful Simon & Ed Crisford yard with Jack Mitchell up — completely unexposed, style unknown, but connections suggest a horse capable enough to run well fresh; must be respected on unknown profile alone.

runners_data.name: Electric Gambler
runners_data.note: Jason Watson partners this Jonjo & AJ O'Neill-trained three-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination — pushed into a midfield slot by field saturation at the rear, so its true stalking instincts may be partially frustrated here; 55 days off the track and sole Goodwill form on good.

runners_data.name: Elite Approach
runners_data.note: South African-trained raider with Joey Ramsden — last ran 109 days ago when fourth over six furlongs on this Fibresand surface, which is the one piece of relevant course evidence; style unknown, lightly raced, and the step up in trip is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Majestic Ruler
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Julia & Shelley Birkett, Dylan Hogan aboard — only form came over six furlongs on good at Goodwin, so both the extra furlong and the Fibresand surface represent unknowns; trainer has struck at 1 from 4 over 14 days which provides mild yard confidence.

runners_data.name: Rua Mor
runners_data.note: Sam England's four-year-old brings multiple runs at this track and trip but none have produced a win or place finish in seven similar-going starts — natural hold-up horse who needs the race truly run at him; 76 days since last run and the weight-carrying burden of 136lbs is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Prosperity
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's winner last time out over eight furlongs at Goodwood — the single confirmed front-runner who maps to prominent here but is genuinely capable of dictating; Burke has 4 winners from 32 in the past fortnight and Jamin is an astute partner for a pace-controlling role, though the Fibresand is a new surface.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Spirit
runners_data.note: 499 days off the track — an enormous absence that immediately demands caution — Sean Kirrane takes the ride for Lawrence Mullaney; best Fibresand form was a fourth at this distance, and the hold-up style needs the race truly run to suit after such a lengthy lay-off.

runners_data.name: Savile Row
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's three-year-old is rated a modest OR=80 but has prominent tendencies and could track Prosperity into the contest — came off a 308-day break and has mixed form over sprint trips, with the mile here likely stretching his stamina; headgear includes a tongue-tie and visor combination.

runners_data.name: Sotto Il Sasso
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan debutant with Joe Leavy, no public form to assess — style and going preference completely unknown, but Meehan's 1 from 9 in the past fortnight is moderate; as with Al Jolson, the unknown profile warrants respect rather than dismissal.

runners_data.name: Ze Gucci Poochie
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's three-year-old was tailed off on its sole start over seven furlongs on this surface and has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — Sean D Bowen takes the ride but a hold-up profile combined with a fade-flag and poor debut form makes this a very tough prospect here.

runners_data.name: My Prerogative
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson rides this David Killahena & Graeme McPherson-trained three-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — with the rear of the field already crowded, it ends up mapped to midfield rather than its preferred stalking ground, meaning it races in a compromised position; just 13 days since last run, with prior starts on good and Fibresand giving some experience.

races.paceDynamic: Prosperity is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to seriously contest the lead from the off, Pierre-Louis Jamin should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on the Fibresand over this flat mile at Southwell. The field contains a cluster of true hold-up horses — Electric Gambler, My Prerogative, Rua Mor, Peaceful Spirit and Ze Gucci Poochie — but the map is saturated with hold-up types, meaning Electric Gambler and My Prerogative are likely to race in a midfield cluster rather than their natural rear positions, subtly compressing the field and reducing the gap between the front and the pack. Savile Row is the one other runner with prominent tendencies and may push forward to track Prosperity, but is rated OR=80 and unlikely to force a genuinely demanding pace. With a single, uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable rhythm and a compressed midfield behind, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit close to the pace or in the first half of the field, pick up smoothly in the straight, and finish with purpose — prominent and mid-division racers with a clean passage are best served, while true hold-up horses face an uncertain challenge if the pace fails to truly stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prosperity Dictates Controlled Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Prosperity gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm, controlling pace throughout without pressure.
scenarios.body: Jamin takes Prosperity to the front and sets a fair but manageable gallop, and with no rival willing or able to harry him, the race becomes a procession until the turn into the straight; horses that have tracked the pace and conserved energy are ideally placed to pick up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or Prosperity fades markedly in the final two furlongs, opening the door for runners held up in mid-division.
scenarios.body: A runner that has tracked inconspicuously through the middle of the field gets first run as the pace eases and sustains their challenge into the final furlong; the compression of the field means a timed run from mid-division can be decisive if it is executed cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is brisk enough to string the field out and leave those at the rear with genuine ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Rua Mor or Peaceful Spirit, racing from their natural rear positions, need the race to be run at a pace that truly stretches competitors; if that materialises, a powerful late surge is possible, but the AW mile at Southwell with a controlled pace makes this a demanding ask.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Prosperity sets an unusually slow crawl that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish with runners fanning across the track produces a scrambled result that benefits a lightly-raced or unexposed runner whose form is difficult to weigh; one of the unknown quantities could steal the benefit of a muddling, slowly-run contest.

watchPoints.text: Prosperity must be monitored at the break — if Jamin fails to secure the lead cleanly, the entire race shape collapses and the structured scenario probabilities shift markedly toward a scrappier, more compressed finish.

Savile Row's proximity to the pace should be watched closely — if Harry Russell pushes aggressively to sit on Prosperity's shoulder, the pace could quicken beyond what Prosperity wants, turning a controlled race into a genuine test.

Electric Gambler and My Prerogative are both natural hold-up horses operating in midfield against their instincts — if either rider pushes them further back toward their natural zone, watch for traffic issues in the straight as genuine hold-up horses converge on limited racing room.

Peaceful Spirit's 499-day layoff is a significant flag — Sean Kirrane should be watched in the early stages to see whether the horse travels or shows signs of ring-rustiness, as any jumping out issues could be an early indicator of fitness.

The two debut runners, Al Jolson and Sotto Il Sasso, should be tracked out of the stalls — their early positioning and how they settle will reveal their natural style and clarify whether either could be a factor, given their complete absence of public form.

races.name: Coopers Marquees Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tina's Indian
runners_data.note: Won at Southwell last time on Heavy ground (HEA) over 7f and is an effective prominent racer; Billy Loughnane rides, the horse wears headgear, and the 65-day absence is manageable given the in-form yard; course form is mixed at shorter trips but the 7f-SOF-1st signals she handles testing days and Standard AW is fine.
runners_data.comment: Tina's Indian shaped with promise when third last time out and a winner five starts back, and he has experience over today's trip carrying 135 lb from stall 7; the chief concern is the 65-day absence.

runners_data.name: Willem Twee
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid Standard Southwell experience — 1W5P in sim-going — making him one of the better-credentialled closers in the field; Rob Hornby's booking is an upgrade, 20-day freshener is ideal, but his last six runs suggest he needs everything to fall right late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Willem Twee does bring consecutive thirds to his name two and three runs back, showing a degree of consistency, though unplaced efforts either side temper expectations; he has experience over today's distance and going, and 132 lb from stall one gives him a workable profile.

runners_data.name: Skipper
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose last five runs have almost all come at 8f rather than today's 7f, raising a subtle trip concern on the short side; James Doyle is a strong booking and the horse did win over 8f at Southwell, but a 83-day break and the step down in trip need to be factored in.
runners_data.comment: Skipper won three starts back but has since disappointed, finishing unplaced and ninth in his last two, and 83 days off the track raises freshness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and 132 lb is no featherweight assignment.

runners_data.name: Dixieland Blues
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner with two wins from seven Standard Southwell starts and a 5-from-7 course record; the 326-day layoff is the single biggest query, but Simon & Ed Crisford are firing at 8/24 in the last 14 days and his tactical advantage in an oversubscribed prominent field is significant if fitness is present.
runners_data.comment: Dixieland Blues won last time out but that was 326 days ago, and he ranks eleventh of fourteen on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite the stable's sharp recent strike rate of 33 per cent; he has run over today's trip and going before, which offers some small comfort.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner shows decent placed form including a 2nd and 3rd on soft/good ground at Goodwood; a true prominent type by nature who is squeezed into a midfield map slot by field congestion, meaning Pierre-Louis Jamin faces an early positioning challenge, and the horse's limited Standard AW exposure (3 runs, no win) tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a second and third earlier in the sequence offering some encouragement, Aurora Majesty has experience over today's trip and going but a struggling yard on 0/23 in the past fortnight and modest recent efforts make him a tough each-way proposition from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Valvano
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 5-year-old is raised in weight at 138lbs (top of the handicap) and drops back from 8-12f trips, where all five recent runs have taken place; holds one Standard AW placing from 10 runs and the step to 7f is a notable question, making this a speculative entry off a 141-day break.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in two of his last four starts, Valvano catches the eye on the pick of his recent form and gets the fitness green light after 141 days off; he has run over today's trip and a rating of 102 gives him solid claims, though he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Legal Reform
runners_data.note: Outstanding Standard Southwell profile — 3 wins and 8 places from 15 runs on this surface, including two 7f wins at STA; Michael Herrington's yard is 2/6 in the last 14 days, and the prominent style fits perfectly against a self-defeating pack of rivals; the 156-day break is the one fly in the ointment.
runners_data.comment: Legal Reform won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but 156 days off the track is a significant fitness query, and carrying 137 lb from stall 8 will test his stamina; that layoff is the key concern for a horse who otherwise shows solid recent form.

runners_data.name: Midnight Thunder
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's hold-up type returns from a massive 569-day absence, having not run since 2023; won over 6f on Soft and Good, with his AW experience limited and today's trip slightly longer than his best efforts, making this feel very much like a comeback run.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Thunder landed a win in his last four starts and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 97 underlining his strong claims — but a 569-day absence is the significant unknown he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good heart — won over 8f on Soft 60 days ago, and has placed at 7f on Soft twice; Seb Spencer's yard is ticking over (1/6 in 14 days) and Dale Swift rides; the switch from Soft turf to Standard AW is a surface change worth noting, with only modest Standard AW form on record.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to advertise his claims, though that success came 60 days ago and a return to form will be needed after two poor efforts before that win; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall four is the neutral backdrop.

runners_data.name: Shiplake
runners_data.note: Two wins at Standard Southwell over 7f make this horse course-proven, but he's a natural prominent runner who is unlikely to get that position in this congested field; Daniel Muscutt rides a horse who has finished 8th and 9th in his last two, and the style-fit concern means his chance is contingent on an unusually clean early break.
runners_data.comment: Shiplake has tumbled to three consecutive defeats after back-to-back wins four and five starts back, and ranked twelfth of fourteen on our figures he is hard to fancy here, though he has experience of today's trip and going, and draw two is noted.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Ocean
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's 3-year-old has a win and a place at Standard Southwell over 7f from just five runs, making him one of the sharper course specialists in the field; the prominent style suits the scenario and Marco Ghiani is an experienced jockey around Southwell; the 50-day break is fine.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Ocean shaped well when second last time out and has winning form three starts back, giving his record a solid look, though the 50-day break and 131 lb are questions he must answer here.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a win over 7f at Goodwood on Good but virtually no AW exposure — 3 runs on Standard, 2 placed; Stuart Williams' yard is active (3/31 in 14 days), he wears headgear (t/ce) and 15-day freshener suggests he's fit, but he'll need a truly messy pace to conjure a run through this field.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the weights on our figures and ranked near the foot of the field, Utmost Good Faith is hard to fancy despite bouncing back to win two starts back; he was unplaced last time and faces a stiff ask from stall 14 carrying 131 lb, even with experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Divine Libra
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' 6-year-old has just one place from 15 runs on Standard AW, which is a damning sim-going record for today's surface; hold-up style requires exceptional pace collapse and the recent form string (2-8850) offers little encouragement despite the 18-day freshener.
runners_data.comment: Divine Libra drops into a competitive spot carrying 130 lb from stall 11, and his experience over today's trip is a useful foundation — our rating of 98 puts him firmly in contention as a leading danger. The risk is that he arrives winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Kisskodi
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on good-ground turf (2W from 15 on that surface) but a true prominent runner who is squeezed back by field congestion today; Harry Eustace's horse ran 3rd over 7f Standard Southwell last time which is the most relevant piece of form in his record, though George Wood will face an immediate test of whether he can slot in the prominent group or get swallowed by the field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kisskodi is hard to fancy at the weights off a 71-day break, yet he does arrive in form — a winner last time out — and has experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Dixieland Blues is the lone confirmed front-runner and should stride straight to the lead from the gates, setting a sustainable but not frantic gallop over Southwell's flat 7f fibresand strip in Standard conditions. With six of the fourteen runners naturally wanting to race prominently — Tina's Indian, Skipper, Valvano, Legal Reform, Great Dream, and Sovereign Ocean all pressing for the same ground — there will be a scrappy, competitive battle for early position in the first two furlongs, creating genuine traffic danger between the 2f and 3f poles as riders jostle for rail room. Dixieland Blues, returning from 326 days off but with four course wins and an excellent 5-from-7 strike rate on Standard Southwell going, should be able to control tempo from the front while the prominent pack burn themselves against one another. This race shape favours horses who can sit just off a genuine leader and finish strongly — in particular those who slot in comfortably behind the pace without fighting for early position, rather than hold-up types asked to make ground late against a field that may not string out sufficiently. The field also holds more prominent types than positions allow, meaning Shiplake, Aurora Majesty, and Kisskodi are all likely to find themselves further back than ideal, with Legal Reform, Tina's Indian, and Sovereign Ocean — all course-proven — best placed to actually secure that coveted second-row slot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dixieland Blues Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dixieland Blues finds the lead unchallenged and the prominent pack cancel each other out fighting for second position.
scenarios.body: Dixieland Blues dictates a measured gallop on his most familiar surface, and the congestion behind him among six prominent types creates interference and stops any single rival building momentum to reel him in; his 2W4P record at Standard Southwell and course knowledge make him a serious threat to last home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Finisher Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dixieland Blues sets enough tempo to be caught, and one course-wise prominent horse tracks him cleanly to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Legal Reform, with an extraordinary 3W8P record at Standard Southwell over this exact 7f, is perfectly positioned to travel in second and pick him off; Tina's Indian and Sovereign Ocean also carry strong Southwell form and the fitness to close down a long-absent leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble produces a fast early pace that collapses in the final furlong and creates a gap for a closer to thread through.
scenarios.body: Willem Twee has course-winning form at Standard Southwell and a hold-up profile that could benefit if the pace genuinely burns bright; Utmost Good Faith has a Goodwood win over this trip and finishes from off the pace, though both need traffic to clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Recovers
scenarios.trigger: If crowding at the start sorts itself quickly and one of Shiplake, Aurora Majesty, or Kisskodi manages to secure a prominent position despite the congestion.
scenarios.body: These three are natural front-rank horses mapped into midfield because the field is oversubscribed for prominent slots, so their chance depends on a scenario that requires things to go unusually right; Shiplake's two Southwell wins and Kisskodi's Standard-going form give them residual claims if they do land a handy spot.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion in the first 2f is the critical danger point — with Tina's Indian, Skipper, Valvano, Legal Reform, Great Dream, and Sovereign Ocean all seeking the same early position, watch for interference, checked runs, and jostling for the rail between the 5f and 4f poles that could compromise multiple fancied runners.

Dixieland Blues is returning from 326 days off and is unproven in terms of fitness — if he weakens sharply in the final 2f, the pace map collapses and the race becomes entirely unpredictable for hold-up horses like Willem Twee and Utmost Good Faith who are relying on catching a tiring field.

Legal Reform's 156-day absence is notable for a horse whose entire profile is built around course fitness at Southwell; if he is ring-rusty in the first furlong and loses his prominent berth, his primary advantage evaporates.

Shiplake, Aurora Majesty, and Kisskodi should all be monitored in the early stages — if any of the three manages to slot prominently despite the crowded map, they immediately become more dangerous than their redistributed position suggests.

Valvano's weight of 138lbs (top weight) combined with a step back to 7f after a run of 8-12f races is worth tracking — if he fades tamely, he confirms the trip concern and tells you nothing about pace; if he travels unexpectedly well, it signals something stronger from the Beckett yard.

races.name: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (Div I) (GBB Race)
Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (Div II) (GBB Race)
Gb Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Southern Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f Southwell trip 26 days ago (form: 1/6f/STA) and has solid similar-going form; Jude Fernandes takes the mount and the hold-up style suits a fast-finishing profile, though the 26-day turnaround is fine and the Olly Williams yard is ticking along modestly (0/2 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Southern Warrior brings distance and going experience to the table and has a win in his last six starts, but recent efforts — eighth and unplaced in his last two — give pause, and 136 lb is no easy burden for a handicapper rated 64.

runners_data.name: Orange Emperor
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo wore headgear (h) and has recent Goodwood form on varying ground; the 19-day absence is straightforward but similar-going Southwell record of 0W1P from 9 runs is limited, and his hold-up style will need a strong pace to materialise, which this race may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, Orange Emperor does bring some encouragement — third and second in recent outings show he can get competitive, though a sixth last time out tempers expectations. Has run over today's trip and going, and 19 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Has placed at this course over 6f on good ground but sits here with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92, meaning he is a genuine hold-up horse operating out of natural position in midfield; Charlie Clover's yard has been productive (2/7 in 14 days), and 12 days between runs is a quick turnaround that keeps him fresh, though his chance hinges on a scenario that may not develop.
runners_data.comment: Federal Envoy arrives on the back of a fifth last time out and is yet to win in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; he has experience over today's trip and going, but 135 lb from stall nine is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with six places from 15 similar-going runs, including a win over 7f Southwell; Scott Dixon's yard is in decent nick (2/11) and Charlie Tucker is an experienced claiming rider — this is a horse well-placed to sit close to Starsong and deliver a sustained challenge.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, On Key faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 134 lb from stall 14, and a speed rating of 58 does little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a sharp enough 17-day turnaround showing consistent placed form in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ahead Of Fashion
runners_data.note: Donagh Murphy takes the ride on this 3yo who has been off 63 days, longest absence in the field; naturally a hold-up horse whose best Southwell effort was a 2nd over 7f, and with STYLE_FIT 0.92 she will be running out of character if competing from midfield — the layoff adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Ahead of Fashion showed clear promise when a second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going holds him in good stead from stall two carrying 134 lb; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 63 days off.

runners_data.name: Blackjack
runners_data.note: A 9yo veteran with 14 Southwell starts, winning once and placing twice, giving him the deepest course profile in the field; despite experience, his genuine hold-up nature means he is shuffled into midfield out of his best tactical position, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.93 reflects a meaningful disadvantage here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Blackjack at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, though he has struggled for consistency before that and a mark of 58 with 133 lb to carry sets the bar high.

runners_data.name: Torfrida
runners_data.note: Pam Sly's 6yo has raced predominantly at 5f and has just one Southwell run in similar going from 12 attempts; stepping up to 6f is an unknown, the 59-day break is notable, and while she operates as a hold-up type, the redistribution into midfield further complicates her chance — Isobelle Chalmers (5lb claimer) rides.
runners_data.comment: Torfrida shapes as a leading threat on our rating, and she has run over today's trip and going before, giving her strong claims here off 133 lb from stall 8; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts, and 59 days off the track adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: The Easterby stable has been active (3/30 in 14 days) and this 4yo has a 2nd on this course at 6f; however, with just 1 similar-going run from 14 and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 indicating he is a hold-up horse pushed forward on the map, his position should be treated with caution rather than taken at face value.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Big Apple Jack faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a second two starts back shows he can threaten at this level.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 3yo has five Goodwood runs in the recent form figures and has never run at Southwell; similar-going figures of 0W0P from 8 attempts and STYLE_FIT 0.93 flag a horse whose natural closing style is least well served by the steady pace Starsong is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pair of fifths and a fourth the best he has managed in recent outings, Great Success is hard to fancy from stall 13 carrying 128 lb, and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 7yo is the lone confirmed front-runner and therefore holds the key tactical role in this race; OR 52 makes him the lowest-rated horse in the field, but uncontested control of a steady Southwell 6f gallop gives him a genuine chance to outrun his rating — Jude Maher (7lb claimer) minimises the weight burden.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Starsong faces a stiff ask, with her trainer in poor recent form at 1/21 over the past fortnight; at least she has experience over today's trip and going, and her second last time out offers a crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Massimo Blue
runners_data.note: Trained by Dylan Cunha, this 4yo wears headgear (tp) and boasts an excellent Southwell record of 2W5P from 13 similar-going runs — the best course strike-rate in the field; Kyle McHugh rides and, while mapped as hold-up, the track familiarity and high strike rate make him one to respect regardless of positional constraints.
runners_data.comment: Massimo Blue has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, posting back-to-back thirds last time out and two starts back, though three unplaced efforts before that temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, and 140 lb from stall ten gives him a fair shot at building on that placed form.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's 6yo ran 2nd over 6f Southwell in similar going but has shown only one placed effort from 15 such starts; the 23-day break is routine, Oliver Carmichael is an experienced claimer, but the hold-up style and modest recent form figures (020640) do not inspire confidence in a race lacking a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Tough Enough has run over today's distance and going before, and at 23 days since his last start he arrives in fair order; yet to score in recent starts, but his speed figure of 82 gives him a strong case here from stall six carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Lesley's Boy
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 4yo returns after 62 days, the second-longest break in the field; his headgear (p) and modest Southwell record (0W2P from 15 similar-going attempts) paint a limited picture, and while he is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, Jake Dickson rides a horse that will need everything to go right from an unfamiliar midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Lesley's Boy has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 70 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 63 implies, making him a live threat from stall three; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 62 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Toptime
runners_data.note: Roy Bowring's 8yo veteran specialises at 5f (all five recent runs) and steps up to 6f today, a trip he has not contested in recent form; his prominent style is well-suited to sitting behind Starsong and he won at 5f Southwell in similar going, but the extra furlong is a genuine stamina query — Joe Bradnam (3lb claimer) takes the ride with the yard in reasonable form (2/5).
runners_data.comment: Toptime won two starts back but has finished third last time out, and his record in recent starts shows just one win from five. He has run over today's trip and going, carries 136 lb from stall 12, and steps out after 27 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Starsong is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 6f handicap and should stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting a sustainable rather than scorching gallop on Standard Fibresand at Southwell. On Key and Toptime are the main prominent types capable of tracking Starsong through the early stages, but neither is likely to exert serious pressure on the leader, meaning the pace is controlled rather than contested. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Lesley's Boy, Ahead Of Fashion, Federal Envoy, Blackjack, Torfrida, Big Apple Jack and Great Success are genuine closers who cannot all get their natural rear position and have been redistributed into midfield slots they are not naturally suited to. This creates a race shape where a lone leader sets a steady-to-moderate tempo over a flat, tight Southwell 6f track, which historically rewards horses who can sit prominently just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent and pace-stalking profiles are most favoured here, with true hold-up horses carrying a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starsong Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong bowls along in front at a steady clip and On Key or Toptime sit close enough to pounce at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Starsong's uncontested lead sets a tempo that suits horses racing within two lengths of her, and the flat Southwell 6f configuration means any prominent runner with residual energy can cut her down or steal enough daylight off the turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Starsong Leads All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly steady and no prominent runner can sustain a challenge through the closing furlong.
scenarios.body: A low-key gallop on Standard going rewards the horse dictating matters, and Starsong — untroubled and rating well below her rivals on OR — has enough left to hold on if the challengers come too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected early pace burns off the prominents and creates a genuine closing opportunity for the pack.
scenarios.body: Horses displaced into midfield such as Massimo Blue, Southern Warrior or Orange Emperor could benefit if the tempo lifts sufficiently to string the field out and leave them with a clear run, though their natural hold-up tendencies make a clean run through traffic uncertain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and genuinely out-of-role closers find daylight in time, despite being mapped out of their natural position.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires redistributed horses — Federal Envoy, Lesley's Boy, Ahead Of Fashion — to be racing in their true style at the back, but the field density and Starsong's likely moderate tempo make a sufficiently fast closing split improbable; STYLE_FIT penalties further discount this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Starsong (Jude Maher) has sole control of the pace — watch whether he is allowed to roll along unchallenged or if On Key or Toptime press him early, as any contest for the lead would fundamentally alter the race shape.

On Key and Toptime are the only two horses whose natural prominent style fits the pace map cleanly; if either is squeezed wide or slow away from the stalls, the front-runner loses its main threat and Starsong's lead becomes more durable.

Massimo Blue's Southwell course record (2W5P from 13 similar-going runs) stands out markedly from the rest of the field — watch for Kyle McHugh positioning him as close to the pace as possible rather than settling deep, which his record suggests he runs best when holding a tracking position.

Several redistributed hold-up types — Federal Envoy, Lesley's Boy, Ahead Of Fashion — may attempt to push forward from the gate given the crowded rear of the field; any significant positional shuffling in the opening two furlongs could compress the midfield and affect the run of On Key.

Torfrida and Toptime are both stepping up in trip from their recent 5f campaigns — watch whether either fades sharply in the closing furlong, which could affect the finishing order for horses attempting to pass them inside the final 100 yards.
